Definition: properly, to press, i.e. (figuratively) to distress
BiblicalUsage: To oppress is the verb of the same weight, and it is laid at the door of Egypt, of Syria, and of every unjust power. In Exodus 3:9 God has seen "the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress" Israel, in 1 Samuel 10:18 He reminds Israel He delivered them "out of the hand of all kingdoms, and of them that oppressed you," and in Isaiah 19:20 Egypt's oppressed will cry to the Lord and He will send them a saviour.
TheologicalSignificance: In my reading, the verb is the promise and the warning together: The promise stands for Egypt, for Syria, and for every unjust power since. The promise stands for Egypt, for Syria, and for every unjust power since.
